explanation: Little is known about Aesop himself. Ancient writers, including Herodotus, said he was an enslaved man on the Greek island of Samos in the 500s BC.

claims.text: The fable of the tortoise and the hare is traditionally credited to Aesop.
Homer, Ovid and Plato are not credited with the fable of the tortoise and the hare.
Herodotus wrote that Aesop was a slave belonging to a man of Samos, in the 500s BC (the 6th century BC).
Little reliable information survives about Aesop's life.

evidence.restatement: The Tortoise and the Hare is one of the fables credited to Aesop.
Homer, Ovid and Plato are known for epics, the Metamorphoses and dialogues, not for this fable.
Herodotus (Histories 2.134) calls Aesop the fable-writer a slave of Iadmon of Samos and a fellow slave of Rhodopis, whom he places in the reign of Amasis, so in the 6th century BC.
